tips.comment: Strong Warrior to win @ 2.1. Race simulation shows Strong warrior coming first ahead of U sure Do (2nd) and Veblen Good (3rd)

A race that lacks any depth and should only involve the top 3 in the market. The Easterby-trained U SURE DO has run in higher grade in 2 previous runs and finished 2nd and 3rd, showing plenty of ability and gets a good pull in the weights.

CALL ME BETTY is a speculative poke running for a trainer who has won two of the last three runnings of this race and who in general does well with sprinters. That could be telling as this filly takes on the boys and the 5lb she is allowed could be a significant factor at this early stage of a new flat season.

Letmeseethecolts stands out with a competitive mark and the booking of Joanna Mason. Has run well on the A.W., and I believe that form can be converted to the turf. Last out finishing 2/18 at Doncaster in this class, off a mark of 52. Runs off 54 today.

Race 2 at Pontefract today is the Tommy Hepple Handicap (Class 5) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 2,419 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old colt Detroit Lion from the Richard M Hannon yard, and will be ridden by Joe Levy. This son of Awtaad has some good recent form with his best effort in his most recent over this distance. He must be a top contender today and has to be included.
Ew chance as he ran up a couple of wins at the end of last season on this type of ground. Up 6lb but should have improved and is expected to be better again this season.

Vampire Slayer did well last April/May when second in two runs on the flat. He has been hurdling since, with the latest run last month a bit down the pack and only sixth. He should be fit from those runs and could benefit from the return to the flat with a lot less weight on his back.

This is an interesting race from an each-way angle, with four of the runners making their seasonal return and fitness at this track being a prerequisite. Mr Zippi's best form is on turf - good or good to firm. He has fallen some way in the weights and has been given a chance by the handicapper. His trainer, who runs a small yard, is probably of the same view and is applying cheekpieces today, so it will be interesting to see if that brings out the required improvement back on turf.

Pigeon House ran a solid race when beaten just a length over 2m at Musselburgh and looks on a handy mark based on his hurdles form. He stays well, handles turf, and with the trainer-jockey combo showing profit in turf handicaps (13 runs, 3 wins, 23% strike rate, +11pts @ 81% ROI), he should be right in the mix again.
Venture Capital to win at 4.50. Race simulation shows venture capital to win coming in ahead of Fahrenheit Seven (2nd) and Vince L'Amour (3rd).

Fahrenheit Seven returned from a break last November to a decent C4 third and won when second up. Then had another break and returned last month to a C2 third. I think he can bounce back now second up.
Looks to be on a good mark here after finishing 2nd at Newcastle recently after a winter layoff. Has 4 C&D wins to his name and has placed 3 other times over C&D. Solid E/W chance at least.
Showed improvement after wind operation. Back in trip will be a plus and can handle the 5 lb extra for win last time out under today's conditions.

Ben Haslem brings Wen Moon back to Pontefract, where he has a great record of reaching the frame 4/5 with a win in the mix. Wen Moon has won first time up and also been placed on his seasonal debut, so this is now the time to strike.

7yo ex-french gelding Dream Composer's last win was on his 3rd last run and over C&D. Last two runs can be forgiven as one was a maybe little bit too hot class 2 race and the other one on too soft ground. Will be happy to be back to Pontefract and on faster ground and back with jockey Joe Leavy. Should be in the mix.

Vince L'Amour has won 3 of his 18 starts, winning at Ripon and Catterick last April and Yarmouth in October. He was well beaten in his final start last year, but returning from a break, he can go well at a decent price if reproducing his form from April last year.

So consistent and is so exposed, this 8yo hides nothing from the handicapper and has appeared on the all-weather more than twice than turf. Was seen to good effect 11 days ago, making all to win nicely at Lingfield. That was off a mark of 79, but with a very good 7lb claimer (4 from 8 in last 14 days) on board today, he can run off a mark of 75. Interesting that they drop him back to the minimum 5f trip here, but if he can go from the front again, he looks a player at nice odds.

Had four outings since returning to action this past December. Sean Kirrane deputized three out of the four, winner aboard once. All runs on Standard, however, but this won't find the gelding lacking in current form. Goes off the same mark as last time out and is up in class, so one to watch and have a small stake on.

Still relatively unexposed - made the frame in all but 1 start (last time out in big field Class2 event at York) but still wasn't disgraced, hampered by other runners. If he gets a clear run he should have the pace to take this against weaker opposition & benefits from Joe Leavy's 3lb claim.

Clive Cox ventures 200 miles with 1 runner for this Class 3. It has a tricky draw to overcome but has improved form to his name. First time up after being gelded. Opening mark is 77, beaten half a length by a horse rated 89 now.

Dark Cloud Rising was never going to enjoy that soft ground at York, so fair enough he didn’t fire. He was in decent form before that, still has a bit of potential, and with a good jockey up and nicer ground this time, he could bounce back and run a big race.

SCATTER PENNY needs to bounce back to form on her seasonal debut but her last two races last season were both over 7f so she could do better returned to 6f. She won on her race when fresh on debut last season and she is 1-1 over C&D, a race she won easily by 4 lengths, on similar ground to what she will face here. It is officially 'Good' Going with further drying conditions at the track and it won't bother here if it turns 'Good to Firm' as she won on that too at Nottingham last June. She has dropped 9lb down the weights since last August, the Easterby yard is in form (Last 14 days: 3-14, 21%), and 'fresh' might be the time to catch her.
Good form figures in this class of races. Trainer and jockey combo is strong. Looks clearly overpriced and has value in betting.
One More Dream to win @ 5.50. Race Simulation shows One More Dream coming in first ahead of ifonlytheycudtalk in second and Mrs Trump (3rd)

Herakles ran a bit too keen and didn’t get the clearest run at Newcastle, so there’s a fair bit to forgive there. He should come on for that outing, and now 2lb below his last winning mark with the yard going well at Ponte, he’s definitely got a shout if things fall his way.

South Shore has tumbled down the weights in quick fashion, having spent the last four outings racing at Newcastle (denied a clear run latterly). He was acquired for current connections for £30k last July, and he now looks well enough handicapped to do the business dropped into class 6 for the first time. Family favourite, Torfrida, is very interesting, but lacks a recent run.

This 10-runner race is full of horses that don't look obviously well handicapped. This horse looks a decent bet, being less exposed than most of these and having notched a win and a place from just 7 attempts over the minimum trip. The jockey's record on the horse is good too, with a win off 62 and a place off 64 in his 3 rides on the horse. The horse's win in a class 2 novice on debut is another clue that the horse could well go very close here.
Crocodile Power, if fit and ready and getting the luck in running here today, should certainly be capable of being involved in the finish.

Small eachway tip for Mrs Trump who is returning from a 6 month rest , question marks regarding race fitness but horses from this yard do run well first time back from a rest. This horse already has good form in the book at this course and today, she has one of the better draws , a low to middle draw is usually the place to be over this course and distance. As a 5yo , she should have more to offer so could show some improvement today.

Pam Sly is one of those rare trainers whose record to a pound stake at the dreaded SP still yields a long-term profit. TORFRIDA is a granddaughter of the Classic-winning Speciosa, and she retains potential after just 7 races. The yard doesn't send horses to a wide variety of tracks, and the fact that the operation has a good record here at Pontefract is typical. The drop to 5f does pose a question, but the stiff finish may help.

Partisan Hero showed a great attitude to get up at Kempton last time and is clearly in good nick. He’s up to a career-high mark now, but the yard’s flying and they tend to do well in spring turf handicaps. Should go well again if he handles the switch back to grass.

Livio Milo has won once, and that was at Galway in soft in a maiden 2 years ago. Moved now from Dermot Weld to S England, he could be well placed here. Looks to have a bit to find, but his best runs have been on better ground, and he may come up trumps tomorrow but will get a tariff if he does.

Race 7 at Pontefract today is the Racing TV Sky Handicap (Class 5) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,615 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 5-year-old gelding Finn Russel from the Ian Williams yard, and will be ridden by Charles Bishop. This son of Caravaggio is holding his form fairly well recently and is threatening another win. A dangerous contender today.
Yaajooz is tried in a hood for a first time and may bring about improvement. Yaajooz is having his 2nd run for the Easterby stable and has a fair record when fresh.

Double Digits drops back into a maiden hurdle having only been beaten a nose in a novices hurdle at Newcastle last month. Went very close to beating a heavily odds-on shot there, the first two going some eighteen lengths clear of the third. Trip and going identical here. Looks to have a strong chance of success in this not overly competitive maiden hurdle.
Off To Alabama to win @ 8.00 - Race simulation has this horse coming in first, ahead of double digits in second and Kimjoy in third
Much better on his second start over hurdles in a two-mile maiden at Wetherby. Finished a respectable 4th after making steady headway from two out without having a hard race. Should be more to come.

Ran to form second, beaten 6 1/2 lengths in a maiden hurdle over 2m5f at Haydock latest. Point winner; has experience edge; entitled to be thereabouts. Back down in trip and with Theo Gillard onboard.
New Invention to win @ 4.00. Race simulation had this horse coming in first ahead of Cahier's Den in second and Gone with the Tide in third.

Locally trained Sean Og might be the answer here off bottom weight in this four-horse handicap chase on his favored good going. Returned back to three miles after being hampered by a faller here last time over two and a half miles.
Underperformed in the last races. But this drop in class could bring him right back on top, as also new headgear will help.
Imperial Jade has won her last two races on good going and could win a third in a row after making all last time, where she held on by only a neck after making mistakes at the last two flights.

The Navigator is getting on a bit but did win two in October, with the latest of those being off a 101 in C3. He drops to C4 today with that last winning mark, which I think puts him right in there amongst today's runners.
Only needed to be pushed out to win last time and had a fair bit in hand. So the 5lb rise should not stop him following up, especially as the one he beat into 2nd last time won next time out.

Would've been placed at least last time out at Newcastle after a pair of placed efforts at Musselburgh this season. Remains open to better and is clearly still on a workable mark if things drop right for him.
Ladys Present to win at 12.00. Race simulation had ladys present coming in first ahead of Powerofjet in second and looking splendid in third.

Breadalbane Lass went well here on her penultimate start over 2m1f, good to soft, and looked as if a step up in trip would help. Got 2m4f last time at Newcastle and proved she acted on good. A mistake at the 3rd last cost momentum. Back here over 2m3f and off a lower mark with the rider's 7lb claim, she looks capable of landing her first win.
Martalmixjac to win at 2.50. Race simulation had martalmixjac coming in first ahead of Limetree boy in second and whosmydaddy in third.

Snapped this up at 5/1. Made too much use of fourth, beaten 13 lengths in a handicap chase over 3m at Musselburgh latest. Off a short break; back on last winning mark. Has every chance. Each way value at 5s. 1pt each way.
Consistent performer who stays well and has finished 3rd on 4 of last 5 outings. Should go well again and likely to be there or thereabouts.
Has shown some improved form of late and has finished 2nd in both of the last 2 outings. Will be suited by this trip and likely to be there or thereabouts.
Wee Alki is 5 pounds better off than the favorite here. Both finished 2nd last time out, but Wee Alki can go one better here.

Snapped this up at 10/1. Wide trip down the field in a Handicap Hurdle over 3m at Newbury most recent where went too fast; inconsistent; sound surface suits; not ruled out down in grade. Nice e/w value.
Has four wins to his name, all at Newcastle. Well fancied in both of his latest wins and the 4 lbs increase might not be enough to stop him achieving the hat-trick here.
Although finishing 3rd when trying to complete a hat trick, he still ran a blinder and suggested more to come. This trip shouldn't be any issue and will go close again.

Shaped better than the bare result over 12f at Wolverhampton two starts back. The return to this trip will help at the track where his sole career win has come. Down another 3lb from last time and has a smart 5lb claimer further reducing his burden.

Hawa Jumeirah did the job nicely a couple of starts back and wasn’t bad at all last time, just didn’t quite get into it early enough. The step up in trip could be a good move and she’s still on a fair mark. If she relaxes and gets a decent pace to aim at, she’s got a solid chance of going close again.
Magna has hit the bar the last couple of times, and surely it's about time he got his head in front. He keeps improving and is no pushover, so he can get his head in front here.

Mission In Malton hasn’t made much of an impact yet but he’s been given time and now steps up in trip, tries the all-weather for the first time, and moves into handicaps. Plenty of unknowns but could show more now with a different setup, so worth keeping an eye on.

Pretty Spirited has only beaten one home in the three C4 runs so far, but comes into this handicap debut down in class to C6 on a good opening mark with handy Alec Voikhansky on top, taking off another 3 lbs, and could be worth an EW 4P.

Mc Moan didn’t land a blow on debut over 6f but showed a bit of early speed and should come on for the experience. He’s back in trip now, which might help sharpen things up. With the yard in form and a strong trainer-jockey combo in this type of race (125 runs, 20 wins, 20% strike rate, +32pts @ 26% ROI).
Has shown some promise in 2 starts to date, finishing in the midfield both times. Improvement is still likely and holds an each-way chance.
Won last time out, and a 4lb rise won't stop him as it looks like he still has something in hand when stepping up to 7f last time.

ELIZA BENNET is yet to run this year but is better looking than most being a Kodiac filly and has top AW jockey Daniel Muscutt on board to boost. Daniel has a near 20% win rate in the last 14 days and this could be another close one here.

Veraison did too much too soon over 8f here last time but is usually a solid type and the drop back in trip should suit better. First-time hood could help settle him and the jockey booking stands out, especially with their good record together in handicaps (35 runs, 4 wins, 11% strike rate, +21pts @ 60pts ROI).

DELICACY drops in grade and in trip both which can see her in a better light. Jockey Luke Morris will be getting some decent rides on the all-weather often making the most of his opportunities and this lightly-raced filly should still have scope to progress.

Biplane won a C5 off a 65 in February, and the same month was a decent second when here off a 69 against the fillies. Although not so good for the last couple of runs, she could improve today back here running against the fillies off a 70 and moving up to 7f. EW 4P.
Has only had 3 runs, with the best performance coming on the 2nd start when finishing 2nd. Not seen since May last year, but enters handicap company on a competitive mark. Holds an each-way chance.

Nazuki looked a cut above when bolting up by 3 lengths here last time and that form’s worked out well since. She’s fresh off a break but the vibes are strong again, and with a trainer jockey combo that does well in these races (19 runs, 4 wins, 21% strike rate, +11pts @ 59% ROI), she’s very much the one to beat.

I will be siding with Vamp here despite the likes of an odds on favourite in the field at the time of writing that being rival Nazuki however Vamp can easily deny the odds on favourite here as rival Nazuki is under a penalty ensuring he won't have things as easy this time out and he is also returning from a 147 day absence on the other side the daughter of Mehmas Vamp arrives here holding a clear edge on fitness having had her first run as a 3yo returning from a break 15 days ago at Wolverhampton and she looked a lot more strongly built on her return and shaped with plenty of promise entitled to strip fitter with that run under her belt now stepping up in trip that most certainly being a wise move by her connections as it can unlock further improvement R Hughes's inmate is more than capable of putting this class 5 Novice Stakes race straight to bed with jockey Billy Loughnane taking the ride . Respected .
Once raced 3-year-old, well supported but unplaced on debut in October on heavy turf. This surface should suit better. Could go well for the top team of Hollie Doyle/Archie Watson.

American Treasure ran a promising race on debut at Kempton, staying on well for third in a strongly run contest. With that experience under her belt and the top jockey sticking around, she looks the main danger to the favourite and should improve plenty. SC Williams & Rossa Ryan in AW non-handicaps: 18 runs, 5 wins (28%), 9 placed (50%), +7pts @ 37% ROI.

Disclosure finally got off the mark at Lingfield last time, winning with a bit in hand and looking like there’s more to come. He should strip fitter for that and with the yard in good form and a solid trainer jockey combo (58 runs, 19 wins (33%), +15pts @ 26% ROI), he’s a live threat to follow up.
Could repeat history again with a strong placing record at Southwell. This horse has recently won and placed 5 times prior.
Track regular, won here early in the year and better than bare results since. Has a good claimer on board taking 5 off. Should go well at a venue that suits.

Returned to form on his first start since a wind op last time out. This is a weaker contest and is down another couple of pounds. Rossa Ryan has only had a couple of rides for Steph Hollinshead resulting in a first and second.

An open-looking basement handicap where Timebar appeals at a big-looking 14/1. He is stepping up in trip, which looks a major plus (has been staying on over shorter trips). He has dropped just about a stone in his last 5 races, and this does look like a very weak contest.

Mr. Stanley remains a maiden after 29 races, which is rather discouraging, to say the least. However, for only the second time, he was stepped up to a mile last time out and appeared to show good stamina to finish a 3/4 length second. The trainer is keeping him at the mile, and he runs off the same mark. A reproduction of that effort might see him make the frame. Luke Morris rides again.
Won over C&D twice off a higher mark and stayed on for 5th LTO at Wolverhampton. If there's an early pace battle the race could open up for him to run into a place.

Philanthropist was well backed and did it nicely at Newcastle last time, winning with a bit in hand. The form hasn’t been boosted much since, but he’s unexposed and looked like there’s more to come. Worth keeping on side now tackling handicaps.

Platinum Crystal did well when winning on the return from a short break with Kevin Stott for the first time. She should still be improving now, second up, while retaining Kevin and could be ready for another go at 7f.

3-year-old gelding who finished unplaced in 3 starts last year, but ran to a similar level each time (RPRs 67, 69, and 67). He has been gelded since his last run and may be capable of better form on his handicap debut.

Despite lacking a recent run, the vibes are quite good for Nahash, and at the price, he is interesting especially since Prince of India's race is not working out so well. Nahash won his maiden without being extended and was then entered in a very valuable class 2 at York in October. By then the ground had gone and he ran no sort of race. Returning to the all weather should be ideal for his class 4 handicap debut.

Stapleford Park looked well suited by the trip when getting up late at Chester and showed a good attitude under pressure. The form has taken a few knocks but she’s unexposed, and if she handles the switch to the all-weather after a break, she could still be in the mix. Trainer and jockey go well together in these races (75 runs, 17 wins (23%), +59pts @ 79% ROI).
Align The Stars returns a gelding on his season return. Trainer Charlie Johnston has high hopes of Align The Stars being a Group class stayer.
